group: Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk
question:
Patient note:
A 67-year-old woman was seen this morning in the ambulatory anesthesia assessment unit at the request of the otolaryngology service, three days before a planned elective total thyroidectomy for a 3.2-cm papillary carcinoma confined to the right lobe that was discovered on work-up for persistent dysphonia; the operative team anticipates a two-hour supine procedure with cervical extension, modest blood loss, and overnight observation on a monitored surgical floor. She ambulated from the parking structure without assistance and reports that she routinely walks her dog briskly for 30 minutes each evening and manages household chores, including carrying laundry up one flight, without shortness of breath or lower-extremity swelling. Twelve years ago, while on vacation, she experienced sudden substernal pressure radiating to the left jaw while climbing a hill; coronary angiography at that time revealed a 90 % mid-left anterior descending lesion successfully treated with a drug-eluting stent, after which she completed cardiac rehabilitation and has remained free of chest discomfort, unplanned cardiology visits, or repeat revascularization. Follow-up exercise treadmill imaging performed eight months ago to investigate atypical palpitations demonstrated excellent functional capacity to 9 metabolic equivalents without inducible perfusion defects, and a contemporaneous transthoracic echocardiogram described a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60 % with normal diastolic filling and no valvular abnormalities. She has never been hospitalized for fluid overload, uses only one pillow at night, and denies orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or ankle edema. Past medical history is notable for well-controlled hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diet-managed type 2 diabetes first diagnosed five years ago after an elevated screening hemoglobin A1c of 6.8 %; she has never required injectable glucose-lowering therapy. There is no personal history of stroke, transient neurologic symptoms, carotid procedures, peripheral arterial interventions, or chronic kidney disease. Her daily medications include metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, rosuvastatin 20 mg, low-dose aspirin, vitamin D, and a calcium supplement; she takes no insulin or other injectable agents and has no drug allergies. She quit smoking more than three decades ago after a 15-pack-year exposure, enjoys a glass of white wine with dinner twice weekly, and denies illicit substance use. Family history reveals a brother with coronary bypass surgery in his fifties and a mother who died of colon cancer in her seventies. Review of systems is otherwise negative for exertional syncope, palpitations with exertion, claudication, unexplained weight loss, fevers, or night sweats. On examination she appears relaxed and in no distress, body mass index 26 kg/m². Vital signs seated in the right arm are blood pressure 124/68 mm Hg, heart rate 62 beats per minute and regular, respiratory rate 14, oxygen saturation 98 % breathing ambient air, and oral temperature 36.5 °C. Jugular venous pulsation is not elevated, carotid pulses are brisk without bruits, the apical impulse is localized and nondisplaced, and auscultation reveals crisp S1 and S2 without gallops, murmurs, or rubs. Lungs are clear to bases, the abdomen is soft and nontender with no organomegaly, and distal pulses are 2+ without edema. Neck examination demonstrates a well-circumscribed thyroid nodule that moves on deglutition and no cervical lymphadenopathy. Neurologic testing shows intact cranial nerves, normal strength, and symmetrical reflexes. Pre-operative laboratory studies drawn an hour before the visit reveal hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, hematocrit 40 %, platelet count 235 × 10⁹/L, white blood cell count 6.2 × 10⁹/L, sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, chloride 102 mmol/L, bicarbonate 25 mmol/L, blood urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 0.95 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate exceeding 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Fasting plasma glucose measured simultaneously is 112 mg/dL, and her most recent glycated hemoglobin two weeks ago at the endocrinology clinic was 6.7 %. Coagulation profile shows an INR of 1.0 and activated partial thromboplastin time within reference range. Twelve-lead electrocardiogram obtained today demonstrates normal sinus rhythm at 60 beats per minute, Q waves in leads V1-V2 consistent with the prior anterior infarction, and no acute ST-segment changes. Upright chest radiograph shows clear lung fields and a normal cardiac silhouette. Airway assessment by anesthesia identifies a Mallampati class II view with good cervical extension, intact dentition, and a thyromental distance of 7 cm; a reinforced endotracheal tube and intermittent nerve monitoring are planned. She has been instructed to continue the beta-blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, statin, and antiplatelet therapy up to and including the morning of surgery, to hold solid food after midnight while allowing clear liquids until two hours before arrival, and to bring home glucometer readings for perioperative glucose management. After a detailed discussion of potential complications—bleeding, hoarseness, hypocalcemia, wound infection, and perioperative cardiac events—the patient verbalized understanding and expressed readiness to proceed with the scheduled operation.

Question: What is the patient's score of the Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) assigns 1 point for each of six preoperative risk factors:
- High-risk surgery: Thyroidectomy is not intraperitoneal, intrathoracic, or suprainguinal vascular surgery: 0.
- Ischemic heart disease: Prior anterior infarction with residual Q waves qualifies despite her current absence of angina: 1.
- Heart failure history: None reported; no history of congestion: 0.
- Cerebrovascular disease: No prior stroke or TIA: 0.
- Preoperative insulin treatment: Diabetes is diet-controlled: 0.
- Serum creatinine >2.0 mg/dL: Creatinine is 0.95 mg/dL: 0.
RCRI = 0 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 1.
Final answer: 1
